title: Rethink persona storage — not a workaround
description: The current design bundles user-created and bundled packs in the same skill directory, which gets wiped on plugin updates. The proposed ~/.personify/ split with a blocklist is a workaround. Need a structural solution: consider personas as first-class installable resources independent of the skill bundle, a proper CRUD interface, or a platform-native data layer that survives updates.
design:
Two-directory overlay model (canonical pattern from XDG spec, VS Code extensions, Homebrew).

MANAGED DIRECTORIES (ephemeral — wiped on plugin update, rebuilt by build script):
  Claude Code:  ~/.claude/plugins/cache/personify/skills/<skill>/references/personality-packs/
  Codex:        ~/.codex/plugins/cache/personify/skills/<skill>/references/personality-packs/
  Gemini CLI:   <gemini-extension-dir>/personify/skills/<skill>/references/personality-packs/
  OpenCode:     ~/.config/opencode/skills/<skill>/references/personality-packs/
  Pi:           ~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/icherniukh/personify/pi/skills/<skill>/references/personality-packs/

USER-OWNED DIRECTORIES (persistent — never touched by any plugin update):
  Personas:     ~/.local/share/personify/personas/   (XDG_DATA_HOME/personify/personas/)
                  - All user-created packs (extract-persona writes here)
                  - User overrides of bundled packs (same id shadows the bundled file)
  Config:       ~/.config/personify/hidden.yaml      (XDG_CONFIG_HOME/personify/)
                  - Tombstone list of bundled pack IDs to suppress from listing

RESOLUTION ALGORITHM (runs in list-personas and all entrypoints):
  1. Load all bundled packs from the skill's references/personality-packs/ dir
  2. Load all user packs from XDG_DATA_HOME/personify/personas/
  3. Merge: user pack with same id overrides bundled pack
  4. Apply tombstone: skip any id present in hidden.yaml
  5. Return merged, filtered list

CRUD SEMANTICS:
  Create:              extract-persona writes to XDG_DATA_HOME/personify/personas/
  Update (user pack):  extract-persona with same subject overwrites existing file
  Update (bundled):    user copies bundled file to user dir, edits there — overrides on next list
  Delete (user pack):  remove file from XDG_DATA_HOME/personify/personas/
  Hide (bundled):      append id to hidden.yaml; manage-persona skill handles this
  Restore (hidden):    remove id from hidden.yaml

FILES CHANGED WHEN IMPLEMENTED:
  src/skills/list-personas/SKILL.md          — document two-dir discovery, update helper script path
  src/skills/extract-persona/SKILL.md        — direct writes to XDG user dir, not skill dir
  scripts/persona_list.py (and bundled copy) — scan both dirs, apply tombstone
  NEW src/skills/manage-persona/SKILL.md     — delete, hide, restore operations

WINDOWS PATHS:
  User personas: %LOCALAPPDATA%/personify/personas/
  Config:        %APPDATA%/personify/hidden.yaml

title: Clarify personify vs system prompt and injection effectiveness
description: Write clear documentation on how personify differs from simply prepending a system prompt. Document exactly how and when the persona is injected across platforms. Research whether there is a more effective injection mechanism than the current Persona Activation Packet approach.
notes: Research (2026-05-15) found that Personify's injection is architecturally distinct from a system prompt in one key way: skill-based lazy injection means the persona costs zero tokens when not invoked. SoulSpec/CLAUDE.md injection is always-on — pays tokens on every tool call. The PAP (Persona Activation Packet) concept and per-reply drift correction via 4 self-check questions in use-persona SKILL.md are Personify-invented — no equivalent found in any other system. The drift correction is the mechanism that makes it more than a verbose system prompt. Key empirical question still open: does the PAP + self-check actually hold fidelity better than a plain 'respond like X' prompt? This needs benchmarking against the jesse/sam/yoda test cases.

title: Design persona maintenance and refresh workflow
description:
Research and design a maintenance process for keeping persona packs accurate, expressive, and current over time.

Why this exists:
- Persona packs should be living assets, not one-time extractions.
- The system should be able to inspect transcripts or prior model outputs, compare them against the persona pack, and identify where the pack is weak, stale, repetitive, or missing important behavioral detail.
- For public personas, the workflow should support refreshing public information and processing new source material so packs stay up to date without losing provenance or becoming rumor-driven.

Capabilities to research/design:
- Transcript review: read user/assistant transcripts, identify persona drift, weak activation, repetitive phrasing, missed reasoning habits, or overdone style markers.
- Pack review: inspect existing YAML fields against the personality-pack contract and persona-evaluation criteria.
- Research refresh: search for new public interviews, writing, performances, talks, posts, or other source material relevant to the persona.
- Gap detection: identify claims, traits, catchphrases, reasoning habits, or public-context changes that were not covered in the original extraction.
- Patch proposal: produce concrete pack edits with citations/provenance and a rationale for each change.
- Review gates: keep human approval before changing canonical packs, especially for public/person-based personas.

Design questions to resolve:
- What inputs should the maintenance workflow accept: transcript files, chat exports, persona ids, source URLs, date ranges, or freshness policies?
- How should it separate observed behavior problems from new public-source research?
- How should provenance be stored for newly added material and removed/updated claims?
- How often should refresh happen, and should it be manual, scheduled, or triggered by failed evaluation cases?
- How should the system avoid overfitting packs to one transcript or chasing low-quality public chatter?

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented maintenance workflow exists for transcript-driven and research-driven persona improvement.
- The design preserves personas as data assets and avoids per-persona wrapper logic.
- The workflow emits proposed YAML diffs or structured patch plans before modifying canonical packs.
- Public-info refresh requires source citations and records what changed since the previous pack version.
- At least one fixture or example demonstrates reading a transcript, finding pack-improvement opportunities, and producing a cited update proposal.

title: Add automatic persona selection modes
description:
Implement a scalable persona selection layer that can choose a persona automatically instead of requiring the user to always name one.

Why this exists:
- Users may want a useful persona chosen for the task, or a random/personality-shuffle mode, without manually browsing the catalog every time.
- The architecture should support diverse, flexible parameters over time rather than a one-off random picker.

Initial modes to consider:
- `auto`: situation-dependent selection based on task type, requested tone, domain, risk level, and available persona metadata.
- `random`: choose from eligible discovered packs, with optional seed/reproducibility and exclusion filters.
- `weighted`: choose from configured weights, recency, favorites, or task affinity.
- `constraints`: support parameters such as intensity, domain fit, novelty, exclude/include ids, safe-for-work tone, concise vs expansive, analytical vs playful.

Design questions to resolve:
- What metadata belongs in persona packs versus a separate selection profile/index?
- How should selection explain itself without overloading the user?
- Should auto-selection run only when explicitly requested, or can users configure it as a session default?
- How should deterministic tests avoid flaky random behavior?

Acceptance criteria:
- There is a selector abstraction that takes task/context plus selection parameters and returns a persona id plus rationale.
- Random mode is deterministic under a seed for tests.
- Auto mode is designed around metadata/affinity rather than hardcoded persona names.
- The system keeps persona packs as data assets and does not introduce per-persona command branches.
- Documentation shows example workflows for explicit, auto, and random selection.

title: Add persona-aware subagent spawning workflow
description:
Add a command/feature that spawns a Claude subagent, and later other host subagents, for a specific task while carrying the selected Personify persona into the delegated context.

Why this exists:
- Users should be able to delegate a task to Claude or another agent without losing the active or chosen persona.
- The trigger pattern should be convenient enough to use naturally, but explicit enough that it does not accidentally spawn agents.
- The design should preserve Personify's platform-neutral source model: Claude/Codex/Gemini surfaces are generated outputs, not separate authored forks.

Design questions to resolve:
- What is the most ergonomic trigger syntax? Candidate shapes: `with <persona> ask claude <task>`, `ask claude as <persona>: <task>`, `spawn claude --persona <id> -- <task>`, or a skill-style phrase like `delegate this to Claude as Sam Harris`.
- Should this use the current active session persona by default, require an explicit persona, or support both?
- How should the Persona Activation Packet be passed to the delegated agent so task instructions remain first and persona overlay second?
- How should the same abstraction scale beyond Claude to Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, or local agent adapters?

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented trigger/workflow exists for spawning a host subagent with a chosen persona.
- Claude is the first supported target, but the command/design names a host-neutral adapter boundary.
- The delegated prompt includes the task plus the selected persona activation packet in the correct composition order.
- The feature does not require per-persona wrapper skills.
- Tests or fixture checks cover at least one Claude delegation example and one future-host-neutral rendering path.

title: Iterate over and release persona schema v1
description: Review the current personality-pack-contract.md and YAML schema. Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and missing fields. Finalize and document schema v1 as a stable contract that community contributors can target.
notes: Research (2026-05-15) landscape: (1) SoulSpec v0.5 (clawsouls) — soul.json manifest + free-form SOUL.md prose. 10 stars, 6 actual registry souls despite '80+' marketing. Format is less expressive than Personify YAML — no typed fields. Could add soul.json as thin discovery manifest on top of existing YAML without format migration. (2) rokoss21/soul.md (277 stars) — RFC-style YAML spec with inheritance via extends/mixins, profiles, normative merge semantics, conformance tests. Most technically rigorous spec in the space. No registry yet. Worth tracking before finalizing schema v1 — our typed field approach is compatible with their direction. (3) aaronjmars/soul.md (492 stars) — prose-only personal profile builder, large community, not a structured format. Recommendation: align with rokoss21/soul.md direction (typed YAML, inheritance), optionally wrap with soul.json for registry discoverability. Do not migrate to SoulSpec prose format.
